name: Chicken Khao Soi (Thai Curry Noodle Soup)
why: Khao soi is the dish that made Northern Thai food famous worldwide — a fiery, coconut-rich curry over thick egg noodles, topped with crispy fried noodles, pickled mustard greens and chilli flakes. A perfect late-September bowl that hits every note Martin likes: bold Thai spice, umami depth, and a technique twist (the double-noodle texture).
author: Henry
ingredients: 3 cups coconut milk, divided (1½ cups + 1¾ cups)
3 tbsp + 1 tsp red curry paste (Mae Ploy or Maesri)
1½ tbsp yellow curry powder (kathi phrik gai if you can find it)
2 lb fresh egg noodles (thick, for khao soi if available)

steps: Wash the drumsticks and score each one twice on the meaty side — it helps the flavour penetrate.
Set aside 1½ cups (300 ml) of coconut milk, and keep the remaining 1¾ cups (420 ml) ready.
In a wok or large pot, simmer the 1½ cups of coconut milk over medium heat until it thickens and the oil starts to separate — this is the classic Thai technique for blooming the paste.
Stir in the red curry paste and yellow curry powder and mix until the paste is fully blended into the coconut milk.
Add the drumsticks and coat them well, then pour in the remaining 1¾ cups of coconut milk.
Add the fish sauce and palm sugar, then simmer gently for 20–30 minutes until the chicken is tender and fully cooked. If the curry gets too thick, add a splash of water (about 100 ml) to loosen it.
While the curry simmers, heat neutral oil in a separate pan and fry a small handful of egg noodles for about 30 seconds until golden and crisp — set aside.
In a large pot of boiling water, cook the rest of the noodles until al dente, then drain.
Ladle the boiled noodles into deep bowls, then pour the hot curry and chicken over the top.
Crown each bowl with the crispy fried noodles, then scatter with chopped shallots, pickled mustard greens and fresh herbs.
Serve with lime wedges, a small dish of chilli flakes and extra pickled greens on the side.

pro_tips: If you can get kathi phrik gai (yellow curry powder from a Thai shop), itsakeypartofauthentickhaosois flavour — plain turmeric + ginger + garlic powder is a rough substitute.
The broth tastes even better on day 2 — keep curry and noodles in separate containers and reheat the curry with a splash of coconut milk. Broth keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
